output.sql:
SELECT p.product_id, p.sku, p.product_name, SUM(l.quantity) AS units_sold
FROM marts.fct_order_lines AS l
JOIN marts.fct_orders AS o ON o.order_id = l.order_id
JOIN marts.dim_products AS p ON p.product_id = l.product_id
WHERE o.status = 'completed'
  AND o.order_date >= DATE '2025-01-01'
  AND o.order_date < DATE '2026-01-01'
GROUP BY p.product_id, p.sku, p.product_name
ORDER BY SUM(l.quantity) DESC
FETCH FIRST 1 ROWS WITH TIES
output.explanation: This sums the quantity on order lines for each product, counting orders with status 'completed' and an order date in 2025. It returns the product with the most units, including any products tied for first. It assumes "completed orders" means the status value is exactly 'completed', rather than the broader is_revenue flag.
